Nothing publicly available ties this specific address to server or data center infrastructure, and this entry does not present a software company's former office as a data center facility.

reading.body:
This entry is not a data center and should not be counted as one. Emailage was a fraud-prevention and email-risk-scoring software company, acquired by LexisNexis Risk Solutions, that consumed cloud infrastructure rather than operating any. The address on file now hosts a different tenant, Safe T Professionals LLC.

The pattern here is a mistagged map point, not a facility. A software company's former office was recorded as a data center, and the coordinates no longer even resolve to that company. Nothing published ties this Chandler address to servers, hosting, or colocation.

That matters for AI because facility counts are only as good as their weakest entries. Arizona has 56 mapped facilities, and only 4 carry published capacity figures totaling 512 MW. This row adds nothing to either number, and treating it as capacity would overstate what the state can actually deliver to compute.

What the data does not tell you is how many other entries share this problem. It covers one address, one former tenant, and one state total. It cannot say whether Arizona's 56 mapped facilities are mostly real, mostly mistagged, or somewhere between.
